rows.title: Eavesdropper detection
rows.hypothesis: QBER rises ~linearly to ~25%; abort beyond ~44% interception
rows.finding: Clean channel: QBER 24.9% at full interception; half the runs abort at f ≈ 43% (theory 44%). With 2% noise the abort point falls to 38%. Measured QBER matches Q = e + f/4 - fe/2.

rows.title: Channel noise
rows.hypothesis: Key length falls to zero near 9.7% QBER with Cascade (11% with a perfect code)
rows.finding: Final key reaches zero at QBER ≈ 10.0% (mean Cascade f = 1.19); 0 of 310 runs ended with mismatched keys.

rows.title: Distance / loss
rows.hypothesis: Key rate decays exponentially with distance
rows.finding: Key rate falls 0.20 dB per km up to 120 km (fibre loss is 0.2 dB/km), then dark counts push QBER past the Cascade limit; first distance with no key: 190 km.

rows.title: Error-correction efficiency
rows.finding: With the standard k1 = 0.73/Q, Cascade leaks 1.14–1.19× the Shannon limit for QBER 2–10% (0 residual errors over all its runs). Mean f by first block: 0.5/Q 1.252, 0.73/Q 1.163, 1.0/Q 1.138, 1.5/Q 1.142; residual errors: 0.5/Q 0, 0.73/Q 0, 1.0/Q 0, 1.5/Q 0. Lowest leakage at k1 = 1.0/Q in these runs.

rows.title: Attack success
rows.hypothesis: Every listed attack succeeds on the paper, fails on PQ-V2V-AKE
rows.finding: 40/40 attack runs on the base papers succeeded (8 attacks × 5 seeds, slowest 3.62 s); 0/40 succeeded against PQ-V2V-AKE (8 attack classes; where a test has a positive control, it is part of the pass condition).

rows.title: Crypto timing
rows.hypothesis: PQC is within the same order as ECC; signing is the slowest step
rows.finding: Signing and verification: Falcon-512 3.7× ECDSA (slowest of sign/verify), ML-DSA-44 3.1× ECDSA (slowest of sign/verify). Signing slower than verifying: ECDSA-P256 no (0.113 vs 0.163 ms), Falcon-512 yes (0.603 vs 0.075 ms), ML-DSA-44 yes (0.499 vs 0.125 ms). Slowest operation overall: Falcon-512 keygen (9.89 ms), done once per pseudonym, not per message.

rows.title: Handshake cost
rows.hypothesis: Ours costs more bytes, adds forward secrecy and revocation
rows.finding: PQ-V2V-AKE (ML-DSA) uses 14,958 B in 3 messages vs PSLAP 348 B, PSRS-D2D 304 B, P²AS-IoAV 1,864 B in 2; compute 2.1 ms vs PSLAP 15.0 ms, PSRS-D2D 18.3 ms, P²AS-IoAV 0.4 ms (EC papers at OpenSSL speed: PSLAP ≈ 0.43 ms, PSRS-D2D ≈ 0.54 ms). It is the only one with forward secrecy, revocation and quantum resistance together.

rows.title: Message size vs packet limit
rows.hypothesis: ML-DSA alone overflows a BSM; Falcon + certificate digest fits
rows.finding: ML-DSA-44 safety message: 2,665 B even with a digest (2 frames); Falcon-512 + digest: 901 B, at most 998 B with the longest possible signature (fits 1,400 B). Messages carrying the full certificate overflow for every post-quantum option (4,304 B with an ML-DSA authority).

rows.title: Network scale
rows.hypothesis: Latency stays under the 100 ms budget up to a measurable density, lower for PQ
rows.finding: Largest density with median handshake latency ≤ 100 ms (every neighbour / same direction): classical 100 / 150, PQ-Falcon 50 / 100, PQ-ML-DSA 50 / 50 vehicles (upper 95% CI ≤ 100 ms: 100 / 50, 50 / 50, 25 / 50). Safety messages only, at the highest density: delivery 73% (ECDSA), 27% (Falcon-512), 3% (ML-DSA-44).

rows.title: QKD vs PQC
rows.hypothesis: PQC is deployable now; QKD is strongest in theory but needs line-of-sight optics
rows.finding: PQC: 124,757 bit/s of key per core, software only. QKD: 8,252,065 bit/s at 0 km and 822,820 bit/s at 50 km in an optimistic fibre-like model, with dedicated optics and line of sight. QKD's guarantee is stronger in principle; PQC is the only option that works on today's vehicles.
